correctness.rationale: The exact quadratic generator formulas and Euclidean gcd identities give possible pair gcds 3,3,at most 30. The three representation possibilities fail for n>=61 by four explicitly positive quadratic inequalities and integrality of x=g/2+g/(4n+3). All n=2..60 are exhaustively decided by the published minimal-triple criterion with n=3 separately reduced to two coprime generators, and five explicit witnesses certify the other positives. The embedded exact checker reconstructs each small-index membership and independently computes 59 Apéry genus/Frobenius pairs; its first 29 Frobenius numbers match OEIS. A finite calculation is not substituted for the all-index proof.

evidence: The 2017 Robles-Pérez–Rosales paper states its applications to triangular and tetrahedral sequences (pp. 1–4); it does not analyze this hexagonal family.
Pascadi §5.5 discusses three consecutive triangular and four consecutive tetrahedral numbers; searchable full text has no hexagonal-number theorem.
The general criterion in the 2015 paper applies to any minimal triple but gives no closed exceptional-index set.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A generic per-input decision procedure is not an explicit solution of which infinitely many parameter values pass. The uniform bound for n>=61 and exact remaining classification are necessary additional results. Published work on triangular/tetrahedral inputs is not a dominating statement about hexagonal inputs.

evidence: García-Sánchez et al. cite the universal symmetry characterization for minimal embedding-dimension-three semigroups; they do not list any hexagonal exceptional indices.
Pascadi provides generic Apéry and genus methods but no hexagonal-family formula.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The theorem gives a family-specific uniform classification, not a new equivalence: its six-index conclusion needs the gcd identities, positivity inequalities and exhaustive finite remainder that the general criteria do not state. Neither triangular/tetrahedral results nor recorded Frobenius values imply this claim.

evidence: The symmetric-gap criterion is equivalent to 2 genus = Frobenius+1 (Pascadi §1, https://arxiv.org/html/1712.02522v3).
The 3-generator gcd condition is equivalent for minimal three-generated semigroups (García-Sánchez et al., 2015, p. 13).
None of the consulted family-specific material identifies exactly indices 2,3,6,7,8,18.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Symmetry, the genus equation, and the gcd/representation test are equivalent formulations of the property. The novelty claim is not a new equivalence but the complete hexagonal index classification and proof that there are no further indices.

evidence: OEIS A069758 contains exactly 29 initial Frobenius values for n=2..30, an example and code for computing Frobenius numbers, but no genera or complete symmetry classification.
A separate exact computation reproduces all 29 table values and checks genus for n=2..60.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Frobenius values alone do not determine whether genus equals (F+1)/2; even a complete finite Frobenius prefix could not rule out a later symmetric index without a uniform argument.

originality.rationale: The 2002 OEIS entry gives Frobenius values but not the genus/symmetry classification; the 2015 general embedding-dimension-three criterion supplies a test but not the hexagonal parametrized answer or any finite cutoff; the 2017/2018 consecutive figurate-number papers deal with triangular/tetrahedral, not hexagonal, generators. The new precise all-index list and integer-exclusion proof are not implied by the numerical OEIS table alone and are not supplied by the cited general criterion without substantial family-specific analysis. Targeted external and indexed literature searches found no covering explicit statement; absence of a search hit is not conclusive novelty proof.
residual_risks: An unindexed derivation of exactly these six special hexagonal indices could exist.
The broad classical criterion permits a bespoke calculation in this family; independence and mathematical novelty have not been externally certified.
The consulted 2017/2018 papers were materially read in relevant full-text sections, not every line of each paper; a remote appendix theorem with a nonstandard name could be missed.

value.rationale: The symmetry/Gorenstein property is a natural invariant of the classical three-consecutive-hexagonal-number Frobenius family tabulated since 2002. The result completely classifies it over all indices and determines the sharp last symmetric index 18. This is qualitatively different from previously solved consecutive triangular triples, which are free, and requires an infinite exclusion argument, not an arbitrary bounded slice or table recomputation. It supplies a usable structural boundary for subsequent work on genus, complete intersections and factorizations.
